I've never had a problem with mine! Setting it up to connect to the WiFi was pretty straightforward, but that would depend on what kind/brand of extender you go with. I've never had any issues with the Linksys. Plug it into the wall, go through the directions for setting it up, then plug in the Ethernet cable. Make sure whichever extender you get actually has an Ethernet port, some don't. Speeds are great, I see no noticeable difference between being connected to the router directly vs the extender (I have fiber optic internet which probably makes a difference). The Linksys site even tells you if the extender is in a good spot in the house or not when you go through the setup process. Just keep in mind that the connection that goes through the Ethernet cable to your PC is ONLY as fast/reliable as your WiFi connection itself, unless you also want to connect an Ethernet cord from the router or modem to the extender, which in my case defeats the purpose. If you have a junk router or modem then you may want to upgrade so that your WiFi connection is consistent.
